explanation: Smart pointers in C++ provide automatic memory management by encapsulating raw pointers, ensuring proper resource deallocation and preventing memory leaks. They are essential in modern C++ programming to manage dynamic resources safely and efficiently, following RAII principles. std::unique_ptr offers exclusive ownership semantics, while std::shared_ptr allows shared ownership with reference counting.
syntax:
std::unique_ptr<Type> ptr = std::make_unique<Type>(constructor_args);
std::shared_ptr<Type> ptr = std::make_shared<Type>(constructor_args);
